name: voidrancho
description: The database layer for Void Core applications: runes and mantles stored, indexed, queried and paged at scale, with edge weights as first-class floats, clustering, and a matrix view of a mantle that learned world models can read. One layer above Core, like Void Palabra and Void Maiz; Core stays pure.
status_note: Founded 2026-10-30 by the author's ruling (VoidCore okf/design/the-transition.md, pillar B). OKF only; nothing is built and nothing links Rancho, so requires is empty. Rung 1 is Void Hormiga's SQLite store, extracted and generalized.
kind_note: A library with no user-facing install, hence `runtime`; the schema has no `library` kind.

interacts_with.name: voidcore
interacts_with.note: Planned. Rancho stores and indexes Void Core state documents and keeps them in step from the SPEC 6.2 journal; every change still enters through Core's dispatcher. Rancho owns none of Core's vocabulary.

interacts_with.name: voidhormiga
interacts_with.note: Planned first client. Hormiga's store (okf/concepts/platform/store.md, 2026-10-27: SQLite, one row per rune/edge/tag, a cluster-paged working set) is Rancho's rung-1 specification.

interacts_with.name: voidsquid
interacts_with.note: Planned second client: its assets.db copies Hormiga's schema (runes, fields, tags, links).

interacts_with.name: voidmago
interacts_with.note: Reads this manifest to build the family compatibility matrix.

provides.effects_note: None yet. Every read or write of a store is I/O, so Rancho is a holiday implementation by Core's definition (SPEC 9).
